validated_results.title: Adolescent animal product intake in relation to later prostate cancer risk and mortality in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of 159,482 men examining recalled adolescent animal protein intake in relation to incident prostate cancer, so the requested nutritional exposure and prostate cancer incidence are both addressed.

extraction.timing: Adolescent (ages 12-13 years) intake recalled before prostate cancer diagnosis, with 14 years of follow-up
extraction.population: Participants in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study

sample_size.excerpt: We used data from 159,482 participants in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study to investigate associations for recalled adolescent intake of red meat (unprocessed beef and processed red meat), poultry, egg, canned tuna, animal fat and animal protein at ages 12-13 years with subsequent PCa risk and mortality over 14 years of follow-up. Cox proportional hazard regression was used to calculate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of total (n = 17,349), advanced (n = 2,297) and fatal (n = 804) PCa.

validated_results.reason: This is a narrative overview chapter summarising the etiology of prostate cancer rather than an original human study of alcohol and prostate cancer incidence.

validated_results.title: Melatonin inhibits lipid accumulation to repress prostate cancer progression by mediating the epigenetic modification of CES1.
